stem: Which item is NOT shown in a company's statement of profit or loss?

options.rationale: Correct: dividends are shown in the statement of changes in equity.
Income tax is deducted to reach profit for the year.
It is an administrative expense.
It is a finance cost.

explanation: Dividends are a distribution of profit to shareholders, not an expense, so they appear in the statement of changes in equity.

stem: Under which heading is the interest on loan notes shown in the statement of profit or loss?

options.rationale: Correct: interest on borrowing is a finance cost.
Distribution costs are the costs of delivering goods to customers.
Administrative expenses are the costs of running the business.
Cost of sales is the cost of the goods sold.

explanation: IAS 1 groups interest payable on loan notes and overdrafts under finance costs.

stem: Directors' remuneration is shown in the statement of profit or loss of the company as:

options.rationale: Remuneration is paid for services; it is not a share of profit.
Revenue is reduced only by returns inwards.
A company has no drawings.
Correct: directors are paid for managing the company.

explanation: Directors' fees and salaries are costs of running the company and are included in administrative expenses.

stem: The tax charge for the year is estimated at US\$12,400. The previous year's tax was estimated at US\$7,800 but settled at US\$8,300. What is the income tax expense in the statement of profit or loss?

options.rationale: The under-provision of last year has been ignored.
Correct: 12,400 + 500 under-provision.
An under-provision is added, not deducted.
Last year's whole tax has been added again instead of only the difference.

explanation: The shortfall of 500 is charged in the current year: 12,400 + 500 = 12,900.
hints: Compare last year's estimate with the amount settled.

stem: A company revalues its land upwards. The gain is reported in:

options.rationale: A revaluation is not a sale.

options.content: other income within profit for the year
options.rationale: That would make an unrealised gain part of profit.
It is a gain, not a cost.
Correct: it is reported outside profit for the year.

explanation: A revaluation gain is other comprehensive income and is credited to the revaluation reserve.

stem: Which order is correct for a company's statement of profit or loss?

options.content: Gross profit, income tax, expenses, profit before tax, profit for the year
options.rationale: Tax is calculated on profit, so it comes after profit before tax.

options.content: Profit before tax, gross profit, expenses, income tax, profit for the year
options.rationale: Gross profit comes before profit before tax.

options.content: Gross profit, other income, expenses, profit before tax, income tax, profit for the year
options.rationale: Correct: tax is deducted after profit before tax.

options.content: Gross profit, dividends, expenses, profit before tax, profit for the year
options.rationale: Dividends are not deducted in this statement.

explanation: Profit before tax is reached after all expenses and finance costs; income tax expense then gives profit for the year.
hints: Tax is charged on the profit before tax.

stem: Loan note interest of US\$3,000 owing at the year end was not accrued. What is the effect on the statement of profit or loss?

options.content: Finance costs are overstated and profit before tax is understated by US\$3,000
options.rationale: The expense has been left out, not over-charged.

options.content: Finance costs are understated and profit before tax is overstated by US\$3,000
options.rationale: Correct: the expense belongs to the year.

options.content: Profit is correct but current liabilities are overstated
options.rationale: Profit is overstated because the cost is omitted.

options.content: Distribution costs are understated by US\$3,000
options.rationale: Interest is a finance cost.

explanation: Omitting the accrual understates finance costs and overstates profit; the statement of financial position also omits the liability.
hints: Accruals concept: the cost belongs to the year in which it was incurred.

stem: An interim dividend of US\$9,000 is paid during the year. What is its effect on profit before tax and on profit for the year?

options.rationale: Dividends are not deducted in the statement of profit or loss.

options.content: Profit before tax is unchanged but profit for the year is reduced by US\$9,000
options.rationale: Profit for the year is after tax only.

options.content: No effect on either, because dividends are not an expense
options.rationale: Correct: it reduces retained earnings only.

options.content: Profit before tax is reduced but profit for the year is not
options.rationale: Dividends affect neither.

explanation: Dividends are distributed out of profit after it has been measured, so neither measure of profit changes.

stem: Depreciation of a delivery lorry is shown within distribution costs.
explanation: True. The lorry is used to deliver goods to customers, so its depreciation is a distribution cost.

stem: A final dividend that the directors recommend after the year end is recognised as a liability at the year end.
explanation: False. There was no obligation at the year end, so it is disclosed in a note and is not a liability.
hints: Was there an obligation at the reporting date?

stem: Match each item to the heading under which it appears in a company's statement of profit or loss.
explanation: Delivery costs are distribution costs, interest is a finance cost, directors' fees are administrative and tax has its own line.

stem: Complete the sentences about the end of the statement.

payload.template: Profit before tax {{blank:a}} income tax expense = profit for the year. Dividends are shown in the statement of {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Tax is deducted from profit before tax; dividends reduce retained earnings in the statement of changes in equity.

stem: Give the name of the total that adds other comprehensive income to the profit for the year.
explanation: Profit for the year plus other comprehensive income is total comprehensive income.

stem: A company has US\$75,000 of 9% loan notes in issue all year. It paid US\$3,400 during the year and the balance is owing. Calculate the finance cost for the year.
explanation: The finance cost is the interest for the whole year, 9% × 75,000 = 6,750, whether paid or owing. The paid amount alone (3,400) understates the cost.
workedSolution: 1. The finance cost is the interest for the whole year, 9% × 75,000 = 6,750, whether paid or owing. The paid amount alone (3,400) understates the cost.

stem: Profit before tax was US\$64,800. The tax charge for the year is US\$16,200. Last year's tax had been over-provided by US\$1,100. Calculate the profit for the year.
explanation: Income tax expense = 16,200 - 1,100 = 15,100, so profit for the year = 64,800 - 15,100 = 49,700. Ignoring the over-provision gives 48,600.
workedSolution: 1. Income tax expense = 16,200 - 1,100 = 15,100, so profit for the year = 64,800 - 15,100 = 49,700. Ignoring the over-provision gives 48,600.
hints: An over-provision reduces this year's tax expense.

stem: A company's revenue was US\$286,400 and its profit for the year was US\$31,360. Calculate the profit margin (profit for the year ÷ revenue × 100) as a percentage to one decimal place.
hints: Use revenue as the base, not cost of sales.

stem: Explain why an interim dividend is not an expense of the company.

points.description: An expense is a cost incurred in earning revenue; a dividend is a share of profit distributed to owners
It is therefore deducted from retained earnings in the statement of changes in equity, not from profit

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A dividend is not a cost of earning revenue. It is profit shared with the shareholders, so it reduces retained earnings, not the profit for the year.

explanation: One mark for the idea of a distribution and one for where it is shown.

stem: Explain why a gain on the revaluation of land is not included in the profit for the year.

points.description: The gain is unrealised: the land has not been sold
IAS 1 requires it to be reported as other comprehensive income
It is credited to the revaluation reserve in equity, so it cannot be distributed as profit

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The land has not been sold, so the gain is unrealised. It is shown as other comprehensive income and credited to a revaluation reserve, so it does not increase profit for the year or retained earnings.

explanation: One mark each for unrealised, other comprehensive income and the reserve.
hints: Think about what has actually happened to the land.

stem: A company earned a profit for the year of US\$40,000 and paid dividends of US\$38,000. Evaluate this policy for the shareholders and for the company.

points.description: Shareholders receive a high return: 95% of the profit is paid out (38,000 ÷ 40,000)
The company retains only US\$2,000, so little is available for new non-current assets or to repay loans
Paying out almost all profit may be sensible for a mature business with few investment needs
Judgement: the policy suits shareholders in the short term but weakens growth unless the business can raise finance elsewhere

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Shareholders gain because 95% of profit is paid out. The company keeps only US\$2,000, so it must borrow or issue shares to grow. The policy suits a mature business but not a growing one.

explanation: One mark for the percentage, one for the effect on retained profit, one for a balancing point and one for a judgement.
hints: Express the dividend as a percentage of profit.
